items.claim: CEO guides Q4 2025 revenue to approximately $125 million.
items.quote: we expect Q4 2025 revenue to be around $125 million
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CFO later restates the Q4 revenue figure as approximately $127 million, differing from the $125 million figure Rafi gave earlier on the same call.
items.quote: we expect revenues of around $127 million
items.speaker: Moshe Eisenberg

items.claim: CEO frames FY2025 as a record year with annual revenue of $495 million.
items.quote: annual revenue of $495 million, a record year for Camtek
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO quantifies FY2025 growth versus FY2024 at 15%.
items.quote: a strong growth of 15% over 2024
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO's preliminary 2026 outlook expects revenue weighted toward the second half of the year.
items.quote: weighted toward the second half of the year
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: COO declines to give specific Q1 2026 guidance, saying it is too early to comment.
items.quote: we cannot provide a solid guidance about the first quarter
items.speaker: Ramy Langer

items.claim: CFO reports Q3 2025 gross margin of 51.5%.
items.quote: The gross margin for the quarter was 51.5%
items.speaker: Moshe Eisenberg

items.claim: CFO expects gross margin to improve over current levels going forward as higher-margin new tools ship.
items.quote: the gross margin should improve over the current levels
items.speaker: Moshe Eisenberg

items.claim: CEO states the Eagle G5 was selected over the main competitor for 2D applications at a major IDM.
items.quote: Eagle G5 has been recently selected for 2D applications
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: COO states the company has not lost market share to its competitor(s).
items.quote: we have not lost any market share to our competitor
items.speaker: Ramy Langer

items.claim: CEO cites the $500 million convertible notes offering as adding financial flexibility for organic and inorganic growth.
items.quote: our successful $500 million convertible notes offering
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO states the Executive Chairman spends 1% of his time on M&A activities.
items.quote: we hire him to spend 1% of his time only for M&A activities
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: COO immediately clarifies that the Executive Chairman devotes 100% of his time to M&A, a different figure from the 1% Rafi had just stated.
items.quote: Lior, our Executive Chairman, is 100%
items.speaker: Ramy Langer

items.claim: CEO announces plans to introduce an enhanced Hawk version early next year with improved throughput.
items.quote: an enhanced version of the Hawk early next year
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO reports repeat Hawk orders from a major Tier 1 customer for shipment in 2026 and 2027.
items.quote: repeat orders for major Tier 1 player for shipment in 2026
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO states new products (Eagle G5, Hawk) are expected to contribute about 30% of 2025 revenue.
items.quote: expected to contribute approximately 30% of our revenue
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO flags a natural time lag between AI/data-center investment announcements and actual equipment purchases.
items.quote: a natural time lag between those investment announcement
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: COO states the company lacks visibility into customer tool utilization rates.
items.quote: we don't really know the utilization of our machines
items.speaker: Ramy Langer

items.claim: CEO states Camtek tools are the reference tools for 3D metrology steps for HBM4 across all HBM manufacturers.
items.quote: tools of reference for 3D metrology steps for HBM4
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CFO reports Q3 2025 geographic revenue split: Asia 93%, rest of world 7%.
items.quote: Asia was 93% and the rest of the world accounted for 7%
items.speaker: Moshe Eisenberg

items.claim: CEO states the company has orders on hand for HBM shipments in the next quarter.
items.quote: orders on hand for HBM shipment for the next quarter
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

items.claim: CEO states Camtek received significant orders for installation this year from 2 Tier 1 OSATs for CoWoS and CoWoS-like applications.
items.quote: significant orders for installation this year
items.speaker: Rafi Amit

qa_flags.question: Charles Shi (Needham) asked, based on orders and customer engagement, how big the second half of 2026 could be.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Rafi and Ramy both repeated they feel 'very comfortable' 2026 will be a growth year with H2 better than H1, but explicitly said they cannot anticipate exact numbers this far out (citing only 3-4 month delivery lead times) and gave no figures.

qa_flags.question: Michael Mani (BofA) asked whether idle/underutilized customer tool capacity, particularly at HBM customers, could be a headwind partly explaining the softer first-half-2026 outlook.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Ramy said the company does not actually know customer utilization data ('they keep them very close to their chest') and stated he cannot comment on it, without directly addressing the utilization-as-headwind premise of the question.

qa_flags.question: Matthew Pan (Barclays, on for Tom O'Malley) asked what percentage of total AI compute investment Camtek thinks WFE spend represents, noting other companies cite high-single to double-digit percentages.
qa_flags.response_pattern: Ramy acknowledged seeing estimates ranging from high single digits to low double digits from others, but said it is 'a little premature' to comment on WFE in 2026 and did not offer Camtek's own number.
